current_hypothesis: A genuinely new graph/symmetry route is to enforce continuity at the simplicial level. If continuity and unit-triangle compatibility force the m-subdivision of Delta(1) to propagate row by row as a rigid lattice triangle, then the whole continuity-preserving simplicial origami family reduces to packing k rigid side-m lattice triangles inside the side-n target triangle with n = ceil(m sqrt(k)). If that reduced graph packing already caps below 10 copies for k=10, then continuity-preserving simplicial origami is not a viable solution family.
stop_reason: Attempt 008 reduced continuity-preserving simplicial origami to exact rigid-triangle packing and found a hard cap of 9 copies for k=10 in every exact case tested from m=3 through m=11, so this family cannot realize the required near-full density.

last_summary.worked: Implemented src/graph_rigid_triangle_packing.py, a new graph/symmetry-based analysis tool for continuous simplicial origami. The script verifies that once the first unit triangle seed is fixed, every later row is forced; across all 12 admissible unit-triangle seeds and for all m <= 20 tested, the propagated embedding stayed affine and vertex-injective, so every continuity-preserving simplicial unit-triangle embedding is just a rigid lattice triangle. The same script then enumerated all rigid side-m lattice-triangle placements inside the side-n target triangle with n = ceil(m sqrt(10)) and searched the compatibility graph for packings. Exact searches showed k=10 is feasible for m=1 and m=2, but for m=3 through m=11 the exact maximum is only 9 placements. Saved exact and mixed sweep artifacts under results/research_loop/.
last_summary.did_not_work: The continuity-preserving simplicial origami family failed as a route to near-full density. The hoped-for fold freedom disappears: row propagation is rigid, so a single ball never becomes a new folded polyiamond, only a translated/rotated rigid side-m triangle. The reduced packing problem also fails at the target density: exact searches show that 10 rigid side-m triangles do not fit into side ceil(m sqrt(10)) for m=3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11, even though the pure area ratio there ranges from 0.9 up to about 0.9878. For example, at the attempt_007 near-full scale m=6, n=19, the perfect ratio would be 0.997229916897507, but the exact graph search finds a hard cap of 9 triangles and ratio only 0.8975069252077562.
last_summary.next_step: Leave the continuity-preserving simplicial/unit-triangle origami class. The next family should be non-simplicial and break the rigid row-propagation invariant, for example via a smooth multi-chart shear or generating-function construction where a single ball image is not forced to remain a rigid lattice triangle.
